## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 In secondary reference literature, mentions of the keyword *āruppa* uniformly concern the wider doctrinal concept of the four immaterial meditative attainments or immaterial planes (*āruppa-jhāna*, *arūpāvacara*) in canonical sutta formulas and commentarial guides, rather than this specific *Kathāvatthu* debate.

Textual reuse analysis generated by DharmaNexus identifies 165 Pali-internal matching passages shared with 20 other texts, reflecting the standardized refutational vocabulary of the *Kathāvatthu* [DharmaNexus]. The closest and most extensive textual alignments occur with other cosmological and realm-related debates in the collection, notably the *Antarābhavakathā* (Kv 8.2, sharing 4,031 characters with segments §2.3–4.8 matching §6.1–6.20), the *Kāmaguṇakathā* (Kv 8.3), and the *Arūpadhātukathā* (Kv 8.6) [DharmaNexus]. Additional phraseological parallels occur in debates treating formless and meditative attainments, including the *Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakathā* (Kv 3.12), the *Asaññakathā* (Kv 3.11), the *Rūpadhātukathā* (Kv 8.5), and adjacent sections such as the *Paṭiccasamuppādakathā* (Kv 6.2) and *Nirodhasamāpattikathā* (Kv 6.5) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language parallels with a score of 10 or higher in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan Buddhist corpora [DharmaNexus].
